title: How to organise the vanity counter | Primary Bathroom
description:
To hold the handful of things you touch every morning and every night, and nothing else.

This is the Vanity Counter in the Primary Bathroom. About 30-45 min.

WHAT DONE LOOKS LIKE
One tray you can lift with one hand, holding soap, the toothbrush holder, and no more than four daily products. Bare stone on both sides of the basin, a mirror with no splatter, and no cord crossing the sink.

THE SIX PASSES
Sort: Pull everything off the counter onto a towel and put back only what your hands touched today and yesterday.
Straighten: Give the daily set one tray, on the side you reach with your dominant hand.
Shine: Wipe the tray, then the counter under it, then the base of the faucet where toothpaste dries into a crust.
Safety: Water and a plugged-in dryer share one small surface in here.
Standardize: Write the four-product limit on a strip of tape stuck under the tray, and tape a photo of the cleared counter
Sustain: When you rinse your toothbrush at night, the tray goes back to match the photo before the light goes off.

THE STANDARD YOU LEAVE BEHIND
The counter carries one liftable tray and nothing beside it.
